title: PRD Addendum: Model intake scope, compatibility decision rules, and pinning exceptions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Addendum to the existing Model Catalog PRD clarifying scope changes for new open-model intake, a decision matrix for when to require full version pinning vs. soft-pin + runtime probes, and a standardized set of compatibility annotations required on catalog entries. Background: multiple recent onboarding attempts for community weights exposed ambiguity around when the runtime must strictly pin to a model version, when a soft fallback is acceptable, and what metadata the platform needs to select kernels, quantization, and batching strategies. This addendum codifies the minimum metadata, defines exception cases, and establishes acceptance criteria and telemetry thresholds for admission and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog intake UI and API require the following metadata fields for every new open-model submission: compat_level, memory_profile (MB), max_prefill_length, quantization_supported (yes/no), recommended_kernel_tag.

Onboarding flow implements a decision matrix: if compat_level=stable then allow unpinned variants with automatic runtime fallback; if compat_level=experimental then require either explicit version pin or a canary rollout with telemetry gating.

Runtime probe job (automated sanity tests) runs as part of intake and returns a compatibility_report JSON blob; onboarding is blocked if probe fails more than 2 of 4 core checks (tokenization parity, KV cache attach, end-to-end latency within 2x baseline, numerics/embedding drift within thresholds).
Console shows a compatibility badge and a human-readable justification string for any non-pinned entry; UI exposes the recommended pin fallback for customers.
Upgrade/rollback policy documented: pinless variants must publish a rollback sentinel metric name; catalog will only auto-fallback when sentinel breach exceeds 0.5% error rate across a 1-hour window.

Automated tests added to the intake CI validate that a newly ingested model with declared quantization_supported does not regress tokenization or embedding outputs beyond the recorded baseline sample set.
Product and Security sign-off obtained for exceptions that set security_review_required=true in the catalog intake form.
Clear engineering owner and runbook for manual pin enforcement when runtime telemetry indicates persistent regressions for greater than 24h.
Documentation (PRD addendum) merged and linked from the intake UI by the release date of catalog-2026.03.
decisions: Default policy: allow unpinned open-model variants when the provider supplies comprehensive compatibility metadata and runtime probes pass automated checks.
Require strict version pinning for models that declare compat_level=legacy or have incomplete kernel/repro metadata.
Introduce a 'soft-pin' state where the runtime prefers a model version but transparently falls back with a published reason and metric when necessary.
Add an explicit 'recommended_kernel_tag' metadata that is considered advisory for runtime kernel selection and used to seed initial benchmarking.
Telemetry gating thresholds standardized: latency SLO delta, token-generation error rate, and embedding cosine drift are primary signals for rollbacks.
Onboarding must include a minimal sample set (50 prompts across 5 categories) for baseline quality checks; failing models cannot be admitted as stable.
Pin enforcement will be an operator action unless the model is flagged P0 regression in which case automatic pin may be applied after PM + Eng approval.
open_questions: Should we require cryptographic provenance (signed weights) for models with compat_level=stable?
What exact thresholds should be used for embedding drift per task category (semantic search vs. classification)?
Do we allow community-contributed auxiliary kernels that modify runtime execution paths, and if so what review flow should they follow?
What is the customer-facing wording around 'soft-pin' to avoid confusion about determinism and SLA expectations?
Operational: who owns the rollback sentinel when a model is used by multiple tenants with different SLOs?
notes: 2026-03-10: Initial draft addendum authored by Aisha; includes proposed metadata schema and decision matrix.
2026-03-11: Technical review meeting with Runtime team (Evan Brooks) and SRE (Marta Ruiz). Runtime requested a 'recommended_kernel_tag' and a numeric memory_profile field.
2026-03-12: Design provided wireframes for compatibility badge states and soft-pin UX language. PM added canary gating flow to acceptance criteria.
Feedback: Runtime cautioned that prefix/KV caching behavior differs across quantized kernels; added probe to verify KV cache attach for each variant.
Action items: Engineering to prototype intake probe in a feature branch; Docs to draft customer-facing copy for soft-pin states; Solutions eng to draft runbook for manual pin enforcement.
Risk: Allowing many unpinned community variants increases maintenance burden; mitigated by requiring baseline samples and probe pass before admit.
Next milestone: Merge PRD addendum, complete probe implementation spike, and schedule canary run for one community model by 2026-03-22.
